title.en: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

text.en: Mandela spent years in prison and then became the first democratic president of South Africa. Today we read his account of that day.

The extract describes the inauguration on 10 May, which was a bright autumn day in South Africa. The ceremony took place at the sandstone amphitheatre formed by the Union Buildings in Pretoria.
For decades the Union Buildings had been the seat of white supremacy, and now it was a rainbow gathering of colours and nations for South Africa's first democratic, non-racial government.
Mr de Klerk was sworn in as second deputy president and Thabo Mbeki as first deputy. Then Mandela pledged to uphold the Constitution.
In his speech he spoke of an extraordinary human disaster that lasted too long, and said that out of it must be born a society of which all humanity will be proud.
Generals who had once arrested people like him saluted and pledged loyalty. Jets flew overhead and two national anthems were sung, one by blacks and one by whites.
He felt the sum of all the patriots who had gone before him. Apartheid had caused a deep wound, but it also produced great men such as Oliver Tambo and Walter Sisulu.
He learned courage from them: courage is not the absence of fear but the triumph over it.
He believed no one is born hating, and that people who learn to hate can be taught to love. The oppressed and the oppressor both need to be liberated.

problem.en: Mandela says 'I was the sum of those who went before me.' If 4 leaders are named after Tambo, Sisulu, Luthuli and Dadoo, how many are named in all?

why.en: They are examples of many patriots.

prompt.en: What does courage mean to Mandela?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking brave people never feel afraid

points.en: Mandela's inauguration was held at the Union Buildings in Pretoria on 10 May.
Two anthems showed a new unity.
Love comes more naturally than hatred.
